source: Seoul National University Korean 2B, Unit 12, tracks 22-31

lines.ko: 스티븐 씨, 오늘 기분이 아주 좋아 보이네요.
제일 친한 친구예요. 어릴 때부터 가족처럼 지냈어요.
참 즐거워 보여요. 언니 옆에 있는 사람은 누구예요?
나하고 제일 친한 친구야. 어릴 때부터 자매처럼 지냈어.
그래요? 언니하고 얼굴도 닮은 것 같아요.
그런 말 많이 들어. 우리 둘 다 이마가 넓고 눈이 커서 그런 것 같아.
아니, 성격은 정말 달라. 나는 활발한 성격인데 내 친구는 내성적이야.

tracks.secEn: Talking about the sort of person you like

lines.ko: 제가 좀 조용한 편이라서 활발한 사람이 좋아요. 말을 재미있게 하는 사람이면 더 좋고요.
그래요? 제 친구 중에 괜찮은 친구가 있는데 한번 만나 볼래요?
한국어 공부할 때 저를 많이 도와준 한국 친구인데 활발하고 재미있어요. 켈리 씨와 잘 어울릴 것 같아요.
아니요, 회사원이에요. 편하게 한번 만나 보세요.
네, 기분을 바꿔 보려고 머리를 잘랐어요.
아니요, 공부를 열심히 했는데 시험을 못 봐서 기분이 좀 안 좋았어요.
아, 그래요? 짧은 머리가 잘 어울리네요. 그렇게 자르니까 시원해 보여요.
저도 마리코 씨처럼 머리를 짧게 자르고 싶은데 한국에서는 아직 미용실에 못 가 봤어요.
그래요? 그럼 어제 제가 간 미용실을 소개해 줄까요? 값도 비싸지 않고 잘하는 편이에요.
아니요. 안 했는데요. 많이 기다려야 하나요?
20분 정도만 기다리시면 돼요. 저쪽에 앉아서 잠깐만 기다려 주세요.
이쪽으로 앉으세요. 머리 어떻게 해 드릴까요?
긴 머리가 무거워 보여서 좀 자르고 싶은데요.
그러면 머리를 좀 짧게 자르고 파마를 해 보시는 게 어때요?
네, 아주 잘 어울리실 것 같은데요.
앞머리는 조금만 다듬어 주세요. 그런데 시간은 얼마나 걸려요?
눈은 아빠를 닮고 코는 엄마를 닮았어요.

keep: a whole sentence someone would actually say
5-22 syllables: long enough to need listening, short enough to hold in your head

carries at least one thing you can only write correctly if you know something — the unit's grammar (A-아/어 보이다, N처럼[같이], A-(으)ㄴ 편이다 / V-는 편이다, A-게), a gap between sound and spelling (this unit's 발음 point is 받침 'ㄻ': a consonant after it leaves only [ㅁ] and tenses ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅅ/ㅈ, so 닮고 is [담꼬] — but a vowel after it keeps both, so 닮았어요 is [달마써요]), or a unit headword
drop: anything with a figure read aloud: 20분 정도만 기다리시면 돼요 would have the learner guessing whether to write 20 or 이십
anything under ~5 syllables: nothing to decide when you write it
filter.splitAtClause: Printed turns past 22 syllables are cut at a boundary the recording itself pauses on — never mid-clause and never trimmed — and each part names its parent in splitFrom.

items.ko: 스티븐 씨, 오늘 기분이 아주 좋아 보이네요.
items.en: Steven, you look in a really good mood today.
items.why: The page’s own A-아/어 보이다. 좋아 is said [조아] — the ㅎ of 좋다 disappears between vowels and leaves nothing to hear, so the ㅎ has to come from the adjective and not from the sound.

items.en: Yes, I have a date after class.
items.why: 끝나고 is said [끈나고]: the 받침 ㅌ becomes [ㄷ] and then turns into ㄴ in front of the ㄴ. Write what you hear and the 끝 is gone.

items.en: Who is this person?
items.why: 누구 ends in a vowel, so it takes 예요 and never 에요. Both are said the same way and only one of them is written.

items.en: We have been like family since we were little.
items.why: The page’s own N처럼. 지냈어요 is said [지내써요] — the ㅆ crosses into the next syllable — and 가족처럼 keeps its ㄱ, where 가족 alone would tense the 처럼 for nobody.
items.splitFrom: 제일 친한 친구예요. 어릴 때부터 가족처럼 지냈어요.

items.en: This is my room.
items.why: 반말 -이야 after a consonant-final noun. Nothing changes in the sound, which is the point: 방이야 is what it looks like, and 방야 is what a learner writes who has not met the 이.

items.en: You have a lot of books.
items.why: 많네요 is said [만네요]. The ㅎ of 많다 drops in front of the ㄴ and only the ㄴ of the cluster is left, so there is no sound anywhere that tells you the ㅎ is written.
items.splitFrom: 책이 많네요. 이건 친구들 사진이에요?

items.en: Are these your friends?
items.why: 사진 ends in a consonant, so this one is 이에요 — the opposite of 누구예요 two tracks earlier. 사진이에요 runs together as [사지니에요].
items.splitFrom: 책이 많네요. 이건 친구들 사진이에요?

items.en: Yeah, I took it last Christmas.
items.why: 작년 is said [장년]: the ㄱ turns into ㅇ in front of the ㄴ. 찍었어 is [찌거써], with the ㄱ carrying across, and the 어 of the 반말 past is the only thing marking it as past.

items.en: You look like you really enjoyed it.
items.why: 즐겁다 is a ㅂ irregular, so A-아/어 보이다 gives 즐거워 보여요 and never 즐겁어. The ㅂ is not there to hear and not there to write.
items.splitFrom: 참 즐거워 보여요. 언니 옆에 있는 사람은 누구예요?

items.en: Who is the person next to you?
items.why: 옆에 is said [여페] — the ㅍ moves onto the 에 — and 있는 is [인는]. Neither syllable is written anything like the way it sounds.
items.splitFrom: 참 즐거워 보여요. 언니 옆에 있는 사람은 누구예요?

items.en: She is my closest friend.
items.why: 친한 is said [치난]: the ㅎ between two voiced sounds thins almost to nothing. 친구야 is the 반말 of 친구예요, and the 야 goes on a vowel-final noun.
items.splitFrom: 나하고 제일 친한 친구야. 어릴 때부터 자매처럼 지냈어.

items.en: You look like your older sister, too.
items.why: This unit’s 발음 point, in the direction nobody expects: 닮은 is said [달믄], with **both** consonants surviving because a vowel follows. Compare 닮고 [담꼬] on track 30, where the ㄹ is lost — the spelling is the same and the sound is not.
items.splitFrom: 그래요? 언니하고 얼굴도 닮은 것 같아요.

items.en: I get told that a lot.
items.why: 많이 is said [마니]: the ㅎ of the cluster drops and the ㄴ moves across. There is nothing in [마니] that asks for a ㅎ, which is why it is the commonest mis-spelling in the chapter.
items.splitFrom: 그런 말 많이 들어. 우리 둘 다 이마가 넓고 눈이 커서 그런 것 같아.

items.ko: 우리 둘 다 이마가 넓고 눈이 커서 그런 것 같아.
items.en: I think it is because we both have wide foreheads and big eyes.
items.why: 넓고 is said [널꼬] — the same shape as this unit’s ㄻ rule on a different cluster: one of the two consonants goes, and the ㄱ after it tenses. 이마가 넓다 is a 어휘 headword and both syllables are written in full.
items.splitFrom: 그런 말 많이 들어. 우리 둘 다 이마가 넓고 눈이 커서 그런 것 같아.

items.en: Are your personalities similar too?
items.why: 성격도 is said [성껵또]: the ㄱ of 격 tenses after ㅇ and then tenses the 도 after it. Two changes, neither written.

items.en: No, our personalities are really different.
items.why: 다르다 is a 르 irregular: the 르 goes and its ㄹ lands on the syllable before, giving 달라. Nothing of 다르 survives, so 달라 has to be written from the verb rather than from the sound.
items.splitFrom: 아니, 성격은 정말 달라. 나는 활발한 성격인데 내 친구는 내성적이야.

items.ko: 나는 활발한 성격인데 내 친구는 내성적이야.
items.en: I have an outgoing personality, but my friend is introverted.
items.why: Two 성격 headwords in one breath. 활발한 is [활발한] with nothing to change, and 내성적이야 is 내성적이다 in 반말 — the 이 is part of the word and not a particle.
items.splitFrom: 아니, 성격은 정말 달라. 나는 활발한 성격인데 내 친구는 내성적이야.

items.en: What is Nana like?
items.why: 성격이 is said [성껴기]: the ㄱ of 격 tenses, and then the 받침 ㄱ carries onto the 이. The question the whole page answers.

items.en: She is feminine and on the quiet side.
items.why: The page’s own A-(으)ㄴ 편이다, and the unit title is made of it. 조용한 is the -(으)ㄴ form of 조용하다, so the ㅎ that is not pronounced is still written.

items.en: You have had your hair cut?
items.why: 자르다 is a 르 irregular — 잘랐 — and 잘랐네요 is said [잘란네요], the ㅆ turning into ㄴ before the ㄴ. Two things gone from the sound, both written.

items.en: Yes, it was hot, so I cut it short.
items.why: The page’s own A-게, and 짧게 is said [짤께]: the ㅂ of the cluster goes, the ㄹ stays, the ㄱ tenses. Track 28 has 짧은 [짤븐], where the ㅂ survives because a vowel follows it.

items.en: What sort of person is Kelly’s ideal type?
items.why: 씨의 is said [씨에] — the 의 of possession is pronounced [에] and written 의. 이상형 is a 말하기 headword.

items.ko: 제가 좀 조용한 편이라서 활발한 사람이 좋아요.
items.en: I am on the quiet side, so I like outgoing people.
items.why: 편이라서 is 편이다 with -라서 on it, and 좋아요 is said [조아요] with the ㅎ gone. The sentence the chapter is named after, with a reason attached.
items.splitFrom: 제가 좀 조용한 편이라서 활발한 사람이 좋아요. 말을 재미있게 하는 사람이면 더 좋고요.

items.ko: 말을 재미있게 하는 사람이면 더 좋고요.
items.en: It would be even better if he tells things in a fun way.
items.why: A-게 on 재미있다. 좋고요 is said [조코요]: the ㅎ of 좋다 meets the ㄱ and the two come out as one aspirated [ㅋ] — the ㅎ is audible only in what it does to the next consonant.
items.splitFrom: 제가 좀 조용한 편이라서 활발한 사람이 좋아요. 말을 재미있게 하는 사람이면 더 좋고요.

items.ko: 제 친구 중에 괜찮은 친구가 있는데 한번 만나 볼래요?
items.en: I have a friend who is quite something — would you like to meet him?
items.why: 괜찮은 is said [괜차는]: the ㅎ of the cluster drops and the ㄴ moves onto the 은. 있는데 is [인는데]. Neither of them sounds like the word it is.
items.splitFrom: 그래요? 제 친구 중에 괜찮은 친구가 있는데 한번 만나 볼래요?

items.ko: 켈리 씨와 잘 어울릴 것 같아요.
items.en: I think he would suit you well.
items.why: 어울릴 것 같아요 is said [어울릴 껃 까타요] — the 것 tenses after the ㄹ and tenses the 같 after it. 잘 어울리다 is a 미용실 headword this dialogue borrows.
items.splitFrom: 한국어 공부할 때 저를 많이 도와준 한국 친구인데 활발하고 재미있어요. 켈리 씨와 잘 어울릴 것 같아요.

items.en: No, he is an office worker.
items.why: 회사원 ends in a consonant, so 이에요, and the whole thing runs as [회사워니에요]. The 이 belongs to the ending and not to 회사원.
items.splitFrom: 아니요, 회사원이에요. 편하게 한번 만나 보세요.

items.en: Just meet him once, no pressure.
items.why: A-게 again, on 편하다. 한번 written closed up means "once, some time"; 한 번 with a space counts the times, and this sentence means the first.
items.splitFrom: 아니요, 회사원이에요. 편하게 한번 만나 보세요.

items.en: What sort of person is he?
items.why: -(으)ㄴ데요 asks without finishing the question, which is why it invites an answer where 어떤 사람이에요? would demand one. 사람인데요 runs together as [사라민데요].

items.en: Mariko, you have cut your hair short.
items.why: 짧게 [짤께] and 잘랐네요 [잘란네요] in one sentence: a cluster losing half of itself and tensing what follows, then a ㅆ turning into ㄴ. Four of the eleven syllables are said as something else.

items.ko: 네, 기분을 바꿔 보려고 머리를 잘랐어요.
items.en: Yes, I cut my hair to change my mood.
items.why: 기분을 is [기부늘] and 바꿔 is 바꾸다 before -어, which is written 꿔 and not 꾸어. 기분을 바꾸다 is a 미용실 headword.

items.en: Is something the matter?
items.why: 무슨 일 is said [무슨 닐] — a ㄴ appears between the two words that neither of them contains. 있어요 is [이써요]. Six syllables, two inventions.

items.ko: 공부를 열심히 했는데 시험을 못 봐서
items.en: I studied hard but did badly on the exam, so…
items.why: 열심히 is said [열씨미]: the ㅅ tenses after the ㄹ and the ㅎ drops, taking its own syllable with it. 못 봐서 is [몯뽜서], with the ㅂ tensed after the [ㄷ].
items.splitFrom: 아니요, 공부를 열심히 했는데 시험을 못 봐서 기분이 좀 안 좋았어요.

items.en: I was in a bit of a bad mood.
items.why: 좋았어요 is said [조아써요] with the ㅎ gone entirely. 안 stays its own word in front of the adjective — 안좋았어요 written closed up is the commonest version of this sentence and the wrong one.
items.splitFrom: 아니요, 공부를 열심히 했는데 시험을 못 봐서 기분이 좀 안 좋았어요.

items.en: Short hair really suits you.
items.why: 짧은 is said [짤븐] — with a vowel after it, **both** consonants of the cluster survive. Two tracks earlier 짧게 was [짤께] and the ㅂ was gone. Same spelling, different sound, and only the ending decides.
items.splitFrom: 아, 그래요? 짧은 머리가 잘 어울리네요. 그렇게 자르니까 시원해 보여요.

items.en: Cutting it like that makes you look cool and fresh.
items.why: 그렇게 is said [그러케]: the ㅎ of 그렇다 and the ㄱ after it come out as one aspirated [ㅋ]. The ㅎ is written and never heard on its own.
items.splitFrom: 아, 그래요? 짧은 머리가 잘 어울리네요. 그렇게 자르니까 시원해 보여요.

items.ko: 저도 마리코 씨처럼 머리를 짧게 자르고 싶은데
items.en: I want to cut my hair short like you, Mariko, but…
items.why: N처럼 on a person’s name, and 짧게 [짤께] once more. 싶은데 is [시픈데], with the ㅍ moving onto the 은.
items.splitFrom: 저도 마리코 씨처럼 머리를 짧게 자르고 싶은데 한국에서는 아직 미용실에 못 가 봤어요.

items.ko: 한국에서는 아직 미용실에 못 가 봤어요.
items.en: I have not managed to go to a salon in Korea yet.
items.why: 못 가 is said [몯까]: the 받침 ㅅ of 못 becomes [ㄷ] and tenses the ㄱ after it. 못 is a word of its own and keeps its ㅅ on the page.
items.splitFrom: 저도 마리코 씨처럼 머리를 짧게 자르고 싶은데 한국에서는 아직 미용실에 못 가 봤어요.

items.ko: 그럼 어제 제가 간 미용실을 소개해 줄까요?
items.en: Then shall I tell you about the salon I went to yesterday?
items.why: -(으)ㄹ까요 is said [ㄹ까요] and the tensing is part of the ending, so 줄까요 is right and 줄가요 is what the spelling would be if the sound decided. 미용실을 runs as [미용시를].
items.splitFrom: 그래요? 그럼 어제 제가 간 미용실을 소개해 줄까요? 값도 비싸지 않고 잘하는 편이에요.

items.en: It is not expensive either, and they are good at it.
items.why: 값도 is said [갑또]: the ㅅ of the cluster goes, the ㅂ stays, the ㄷ tenses — the same shape as this unit’s ㄻ rule on another cluster. And the sentence ends on the chapter’s own V-는 편이다.
items.splitFrom: 그래요? 그럼 어제 제가 간 미용실을 소개해 줄까요? 값도 비싸지 않고 잘하는 편이에요.

items.en: Did you make a booking?
items.why: 예약하셨나요 is said [예야카션나요]: the 받침 ㄱ meets the ㅎ and the two come out as [ㅋ], then the ㅆ turns into ㄴ before the ㄴ. Nothing between the first syllable and the last is written the way it sounds.
items.splitFrom: 어서 오세요. 예약하셨나요?

items.en: Will I have to wait long?
items.why: 많이 is [마니] again — the ㅎ of the cluster drops and the ㄴ carries across. The ㅎ is in the word 많다 and nowhere in the sound.
items.splitFrom: 아니요. 안 했는데요. 많이 기다려야 하나요?

items.en: Please sit over there and wait a moment.
items.why: 앉아서 is said [안자서]: with a vowel after it the ㄵ splits, the ㄴ staying and the ㅈ moving across. 저쪽에 is [저쪼게].
items.splitFrom: 20분 정도만 기다리시면 돼요. 저쪽에 앉아서 잠깐만 기다려 주세요.

items.en: Please sit over here.
items.why: 앉으세요 is [안즈세요], the same split as 앉아서 — and the reason both are written with the whole cluster is that 앉다 on its own is [안따].
items.splitFrom: 이쪽으로 앉으세요. 머리 어떻게 해 드릴까요?

items.en: How would you like your hair done?
items.why: 어떻게 is said [어떠케] — the ㅎ and the ㄱ fuse into an aspirate. The salon’s own opening question, and the one a learner has to answer.
items.splitFrom: 이쪽으로 앉으세요. 머리 어떻게 해 드릴까요?

items.ko: 긴 머리가 무거워 보여서 좀 자르고 싶은데요.
items.en: My long hair looks heavy, so I would like to cut it a bit.
items.why: 무겁다 is a ㅂ irregular, so it is 무거워 보여서 and never 무겁어. The ㅂ is neither heard nor written here, and it comes back in 무겁다.

items.en: How about getting a perm?
items.why: 게 is 것이 worn down to one syllable, and the full form is what would be written if it were written out. 파마를 하다 is a 미용실 headword.
items.splitFrom: 그러면 머리를 좀 짧게 자르고 파마를 해 보시는 게 어때요?

items.en: Would permed hair suit me?
items.why: 어울릴까요 is said [어울릴까요] with the ending already tense; 저한테 is [저한테], where the ㅎ survives because it opens its own syllable. The contrast with 좋고 [조코] is the whole ㅎ story in one dialogue.

items.ko: 네, 아주 잘 어울리실 것 같은데요.
items.en: Yes, I think it will suit you very well.
items.why: 것 같은데요 is said [걷 까튼데요]: the 것 is [걷] on its own and then tenses the 같 after it. The honorific -시- is in 어울리실 and has no sound of its own to give it away.

items.en: Then please do it that way.
items.why: 그렇게 is [그러케] once more. Nine syllables written, eight heard — the ㅎ has become a feature of the ㄱ instead of a sound of its own.

items.en: Shall I cut your bangs a bit as well?
items.why: 앞머리 is said [암머리]: the ㅍ becomes [ㅁ] in front of the ㅁ, so the word sounds like it begins with the wrong letter. 잘라 is the 르 irregular of 자르다.

items.en: Just trim the bangs a little.
items.why: 앞머리는 is [암머리는] again, and 다듬어 is [다드머]. 앞머리를 다듬다 is the 어휘 page’s own phrase, printed under the picture of it.
items.splitFrom: 앞머리는 조금만 다듬어 주세요. 그런데 시간은 얼마나 걸려요?

items.en: By the way, how long will it take?
items.why: 시간은 is said [시가는] — the ㄴ carries onto the 은 and the word looks briefly like a different one. 걸려요 is 걸리다, not the 르 irregular it resembles.
items.splitFrom: 앞머리는 조금만 다듬어 주세요. 그런데 시간은 얼마나 걸려요?

items.en: Your brother looks so young.
items.why: The rule this page teaches: 젊네요 is said [점네요]. A consonant follows the ㄻ, so only the ㅁ is pronounced and the ㄹ is gone — and the ㄴ of 네 is what makes it happen.

items.en: I want to take after my father.
items.why: 닮고 is said [담꼬]. The ㄻ loses its ㄹ and then tenses the ㄱ after it — two changes from one cluster, and the page prints both halves of the rule for exactly this word.

items.en: My younger sibling and I do not look alike.
items.why: 닮지 is said [담찌]: ㄹ gone, ㅈ tensed. 않았어요 is [아나써요], with its own ㅎ dropping — two different clusters losing two different consonants in one sentence.

items.en: My grandfather lives very youthfully.
items.why: 젊게 is said [점께], and it is the chapter’s A-게 on the chapter’s own 발음 point. 할아버지 is [하라버지], the ㄹ carrying across.

items.en: Children seem to take after their parents.
items.why: 닮는 is said [담는]: the ㄹ goes before the ㄴ and only the ㅁ is left. Nothing tenses here, because ㄴ is not one of the four consonants the second half of the rule applies to.

items.en: Who do you take after, Kelly?
items.why: The other direction: 닮았어요 is said [달마써요], with **both** consonants surviving because a vowel follows. The rule on this page is about a ㄻ meeting a consonant, and this is what happens when it does not.

items.ko: 눈은 아빠를 닮고 코는 엄마를 닮았어요.
items.en: I have my father’s eyes and my mother’s nose.
items.why: Both halves in one sentence, which is why the book puts it last: 닮고 is [담꼬] and 닮았어요 is [달마써요]. Same four letters, and the only difference is whether what follows is a consonant or a vowel.

listenOnly: Every track carries a script: the unit pages print them for the grammar, 말하기 and 발음 tracks, and the 듣기 지문 at the back of the book prints the two 듣기 conversations.
